text: In the third round. <break time="0.8s" /> Sandel left an opening. <break time="0.8s" /> And Toms hook caught him on the jaw. <break time="0.8s" /> And sent him to the floor. <break time="0.8s" /> Until the count of nine. <break time="0.8s" /> Had the blow landed. <break time="0.8s" /> An inch nearer the point of the chin. <break time="0.8s" /> Tom thought. <break time="0.8s" /> The fight would have ended there. <break time="0.8s" /> And the thirty pounds would have been his. <break time="0.8s" /> Tom often held the young man in a clinch. <break time="0.8s" /> To rest. <break time="0.8s" /> While Sandel. <break time="0.8s" /> Who had never learned to rest. <break time="0.8s" /> Wasted his strength on wild swings. <break time="0.8s" /> In the ninth round. <break time="0.8s" /> Tom knocked him down three times. <break time="0.8s" /> Yet each time the young man rose again. <break time="0.8s" /> His youth quickly bringing back his strength. <break time="0.8s" /> In the tenth round. <break time="0.8s" /> A blow to the side of the head. <break time="0.8s" /> Stunned Tom for a moment. <break time="0.8s" /> But he recovered. <break time="0.8s" /> And twice sent Sandel to the floor. <break time="0.8s" /> A police captain moved. <break time="0.8s" /> To stop the fight. <break time="0.8s" /> Which would have given Tom the purse. <break time="0.8s" /> But Sandel protested. <break time="0.8s" /> That he was still perfectly fit. <break time="0.8s" /> Then Tom remembered the words. <break time="0.8s" /> A rich gentleman had said to him long ago. <break time="0.8s" /> After he had beaten Stowsher Bill. <break time="0.8s" /> Youth will be served. <break time="0.8s" /> Now that phrase was turning against him. <break time="0.8s" /> And with every minute. <break time="0.8s" /> He felt his strength draining away. <break time="0.8s" /> While his body cried out for food.
